summary.short: Establishes Oifig IS na hÉireann and Ireland's national framework for Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act): single point of contact, AI register, sandboxes, market surveillance, adjudication and administrative fines. Commencement by ministerial order.
summary.long: Establishes Oifig IS na hÉireann, a body corporate with a board and chief executive, to co-ordinate and supervise implementation of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 in Ireland. The Office is the single point of contact and keeps an AI register; it may create regulatory sandboxes by regulation and co-operate with foreign bodies (Parts 2 and 3). Providers may apply for real-world testing of high-risk AI systems, with review rights (Part 3). Market surveillance authorities may authorise derogations, obtain documents and source code, and receive complaints (Part 4). Authorised officers may enter premises, seize products and serve contravention, prohibition and removal notices, with District Court appeals (Part 5). Adjudicators find breaches after a notice of suspected non-compliance; administrative fines are capped by reference to the AI Regulation (€1,000,000 for public bodies) and take effect on High Court confirmation (Part 6). Offences carry fines or imprisonment of up to five years on indictment (Part 7). Part 8 applies fine powers to the Central Bank; Part 9 amends the Competition and Consumer Protection Act 2014 to add AI Regulation investigations.

notes: This is part 1 of 2 (ss.1 to 136). Section 136 opens an insertion of Part 2A into the 2014 Act that continues in part 2; ss.138 to 139 (amendments to the Communications Regulation Act 2002 and the Freedom of Information Act 2014) and the Schedules are in part 2 and are not coded here. Commencement depends on ministerial orders (ss.1(2), 7, 24(4)); no dates are coded. Registry IDs for targets are unknown, so target_instrument_id is blank. Internal drafting points: s.102(2) refers to a finding under section 100 that a person has not committed an infringement, but s.100 concerns administrative fines and s.99 concerns breach findings; s.113(2) refers to subsections (2) and (3) of section 113, which has only two subsections. Entities in the s.78 and s.53 lists are coded from the lists themselves; s.53 bodies are named as relevant fundamental rights public bodies, and their powers are set out in ss.59 and 77 onward. Part 2 of 2 (ss.46B-46R, ss.137-139, Schedules 1-4). The enabling act and definitions of Commission, Office, inquiry subject and Act of 2014 are not in this part, so no legal_basis row is given. Target instrument IDs and LEI/ticker are empty strings because the schema requires strings and no registry IDs were supplied. Schedule 4, para. 15 refers to Part 2A, but this part has no Part 2A heading; the parent Part is not identified here. Sections 46B-46R close with a quotation mark after s.46R(3), indicating inserted text.
